prefs.import.doDefault: Import and use the ★ profile as default
prefs.import.done: Imported: {p} profile(s), {s} preset(s) and {k} global key(s)
prefs.import.intro: Export your profiles as JSON from another terminal emulator (all of them or a single one), or use a .itermcolors color preset or a preferences file such as com.googlecode.iterm2.plist. Copy it to your LordOS home folder (for example to Downloads).
prefs.import.none: No .json, .itermcolors or .plist files in Downloads, Documents or Desktop.
prefs.import.title: Import Profiles
prefs.keys.profile: KEYS FOR THIS PROFILE (override everything else)
prefs.keys.shortcuts: TERMINAL SHORTCUTS (❖ = Super key) — click to change
prefs.name: Name
prefs.file.intro: Profiles, colors, key mappings, shortcuts and the hotkey are kept in a file of their own, so you can back it up, version it or keep it in a folder you sync. Every change is written there, atomically, with five rotating backups next to it (.1 to .5).
prefs.file.cacheNote: A copy of the last good version is kept in {path}, for when this place isn’t there.
prefs.file.back: The configuration file is back. Changes are saved there again.
prefs.file.away: {path} isn’t available ({why}). The Terminal is using the last good copy, read-only: changes you make now aren’t saved. Try again when the disk or folder is back, or choose another location.
prefs.file.backupsNote: Import takes a LordTerminal JSON export and another terminal emulator’s profiles or preferences (.plist, .itermcolors); what you import is written to the configuration file.
prefs.file.chooseTitle: Where to keep the Terminal’s configuration
prefs.file.askMove: Move the current configuration to this file? From now on every change is saved here.
prefs.file.askExists: There is already a file here. Use the configuration in it, or replace it with the current one?
prefs.file.useThere: Use the File That Is There
prefs.file.backDefault: The configuration is back in its default place, {path}.
prefs.file.mustJson: The file name must end in .json.

prefs.rulesHint: Paths (~/prod/*, /srv/**), user@host, host or user@, with * as a wildcard. The shell (bash/zsh/fish integration) or ssh reports the user and host.
prefs.triggersHint: When a new line matches the regular expression, the action runs. In the parameter, \1 \2… are the groups. Highlight: "#text,#background" (e.g. #ffffff,#ff453a). Title: the title text.

claude.ask: Show Claude Code's context and plan limits (5 hours and week) in this bar?
claude.askDisconnect: Stop showing Claude Code's context and limits in this bar?
claude.detail: LordOS adds its lord-claude-status in front of your status line command in {file}; what your status line shows doesn't change. The previous file is kept as settings.json.lordos-backup.
claude.detailDisconnect: Your status line command in {file} goes back to how it was.
claude.unreadable: ~/.claude/settings.json isn't valid JSON, so it was left as it is. Fix it and try again.
claude.connected: Connected: the context and limits show from Claude Code's next update
claude.disconnected: Disconnected from Claude Code's status line
